# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction (see AC9 for the additional finale
  cluster added after producer review). Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

- **AC9 — Mini-boss finale (producer review, 2026-10-29).** On the defeat frame
  the mini-boss additionally receives **20 finale bursts** clustered **in and
  around** its captured death position — 10 anchored bursts (`AC2`) are kept
  and the finale adds a wider, denser cluster on top. The finale fires **in
  pairs: two bursts every 0.25 s** (ten pairs), starting after the anchored
  celebration so the display builds to the mini-boss's biggest beat. The
  finale is run-seeded (no `Math.random()`), awards nothing (AC4), and the
  reward overlay (AC3) waits for the last finale pair to finish animating.
  Total sweep bursts are therefore bounded at
  `n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + 20 ≤ 60`.

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68** – AI should focus fire on the boss (open)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)
- **AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F** – AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in mini-boss reward screen (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muwz5hcv0034h44, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcrbno6003e1ch, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, ac1 (+453 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+425 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvcrav3b0069aij, 0mvcrbisu006nun5, ac1, ac2 (+407 more)

## Appendix: Producer review follow-up (2026-10-29)

The first implementation was **rejected by manual review** with: "Enemies
explode but the mini-boss itself needs to be more explosive. Cluster another
20 explosions in and around the mini-boss, with 2 going off every 0.25 of a
second."

Interpretation adopted (recorded in AC9):

- **"another 20"** — the 10 anchored bursts from AC2 are retained and 20
  additional finale bursts are added, giving 30 mini-boss-centred bursts.
- **"in and around"** — finale bursts are sampled uniformly inside a wider
  radius (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_SPREAD_PX` = 160 px) than the anchored
  cluster (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHOR_SPREAD_PX` = 80 px), so some land inside
  the boss footprint and some around it.
- **"2 going off every 0.25 of a second"** — the 20 bursts are scheduled as 10
  pairs, each pair sharing a start time, consecutive pairs 250 ms apart
  (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_PAIR_SIZE = 2`,
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_PAIR_INTERVAL_MS = 250`). The pairs start after the
  anchored window (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_START_MS` = 340 ms) so the finale
  reads as an escalation, and the sweep now completes (reward overlay opens)
  ~2.95 s after the lethal hit.
- Finale bursts are denser/larger than the anchored ones
  (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_PARTICLES = 20`,
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_SCALE = 1.2`) to make the mini-boss death the
  biggest beat on screen.
- All changes live in the shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper, so `PlayScene`
  and `GymMiniBoss` consume the identical finale (AC5 parity preserved).

# In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget for long clips written outside the served repo root

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite and a
manual long-run soak), discovered-from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

## Problem statement

A clip larger than the 32 MiB in-page probe threshold is probed by streaming
the **written file** back over the capture dev server's HTTP URL, which only
works while the file sits inside the served repository root. With a supported
invocation that writes elsewhere (`--output /tmp/…`, the very command the docs
use to reproduce the memory budget) the probe silently falls back to the
in-page Blob path, and a 5-clip batch then peaked at **661.0 MiB** node RSS
against a documented **< 512 MiB** target — while the same workload probed
through the streamed path peaked at **408.9 MiB**. The documented budget
therefore does not hold for every supported output path, and nothing warns the
operator that choosing an output path outside the repo root crosses a
documented bound.

## Users and user stories

- **As a producer recording a long full-run soak**, I want `--output /tmp/soak.webm`
  (as documented) to stay inside the documented `< 512 MiB` node budget, so a
  soak does not look like a memory regression.
- **As an implementer reading `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`**, I want the
  memory-budget section to state which paths the budget actually covers and
  what the fallback costs, so I can trust the numbers I compare a soak against.
- **As an agent triaging a soak**, I want `probeSource`/`probeSourceReason` and
  the RSS figures to make a fallback-driven RSS peak distinguishable from real
  recording growth.

## Existing state (verified during this intake)

- **Selection policy** (`scripts/capture-probe.mjs`): `chooseProbeSource` picks
  `stream` for clips above `CAPTURE_PROBE_STREAM_THRESHOLD_BYTES`
  (= `CAPTURE_PROBE_PREFIX_BUDGET_BYTES` = 32 MiB), `in-page` at or below it.
- **Serving seam** (`buildProbeFileUrl`): returns `{ ok: false }` when the clip
  path is not under `REPO_ROOT` ("the clip path … is outside the served
  repository root"), covered by an existing test
  (`scripts/capture-probe.test.ts` — "refuses a clip outside the served
  repository root").
- **Fallback seam** (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `stopRecordingAndProbe`
  ~L3052): when the choice is `stream` but the URL cannot be built, the probe
  runs `probeRecordingInPage` with `source: 'in-page'` and records the reason
  in `probeSourceReason`; a clip is never failed for an unservable output path.
- **Docs contradiction**: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory
  budget publishes the `< 512 MiB` bound and tells the reader to reproduce it
  with `--output /tmp/soak.webm` (also the quick-start at ~L56 and the
  diagnostics section at ~L891) — i.e. the documented reproduction command is
  exactly the unservable-output case that takes the fallback.
- **Parent's sanctioned fallback**: AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE only sanctioned the
  in-page decode for clips *below* the size threshold (recorded assumption:
  "keep the existing in-page decode for clips below a documented size
  threshold"); the path-based fallback for large clips is an unplanned
  residual gap, which was filed as this item.
- **Evidence is no longer on disk**: the cited artefacts
  (`/tmp/ah-soak/batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`,
  `capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`) are absent from this
  checkout, so the numbers currently rest on the comment on
  AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES and must be re-measured to be re-verified.
- **Middleware precedent**: `vite/plugins/botTuningPlugin.ts` (~L161),
  `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` (~L586) and
  `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` (~L282) already register
  `server.middlewares.use(...)` handlers, so a capture-only route that serves
  the clip being probed is an established shape in this repo.
- **Attribution caveat (see Appendix Q2)**: the filed mechanism ("the fallback
  decodes … which inflates node RSS") does not obviously hold — the
  `decodeAudioData` work happens in the Chromium page, whose memory is a
  separate process from node's `process.memoryUsage().rss`, the quantity the
  budget measures. The 661 MiB figure is also confounded with batch-vs-single:
  it comes from a 5-clip batch written outside the root, while the longest
  single run in the same batch peaked at **464.4 MiB** and the streamed control
  was a single 600 s clip. The gap is real and worth closing; the cause is not
  yet isolated.

## Intended change (decided — Option C: fix the serving seam, gated on measurement)

**Producer decision:** Q1 = **C** (fix the serving seam, but only once the
measurement confirms the cause), Q2 = **A** (measure first), Q3 = **(a)**
(warn with an actionable hint and continue). Recorded in the Appendix below.

1. **Measure first** (AC1): a controlled A/B of the same workload inside vs
   outside the served root, plus a single `> 32 MiB` clip written to `/tmp/…`,
   so the cause is isolated — fallback probe vs process-lifetime accumulation
   across a batch.
2. **Then fix the serving seam**: make the clip currently being probed
   available to the page through a capture-only, tokenised route on the capture
   dev server (never a general filesystem route), so a `> 32 MiB` clip written
   to `/tmp/…` still probes via `stream` and the `< 512 MiB` budget holds.
3. **Keep the in-page path as the last-resort fallback** for a probe that
   genuinely cannot be served, and warn with an actionable hint when it is
   taken (Q3 = a): never fail an already-recorded clip, but never let a
   budget-crossing path stay silent either.
4. **Update the documentation** (including the reproduction commands) to match
   the behaviour that ships.

If the AC1 measurement exonerates the fallback, stop and re-scope with the
producer before implementing step 2 — the documentation correction alone (the
former Option A) would then be the remaining work.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Measurement isolates the variable.** A > 32 MiB clip written outside the
   served repository root is measured before any change, in a controlled A/B
   (same batch size and clip length inside vs outside the root, and/or a single
   clip), and the per-clip `probeSource` plus `node.peakRssBytes` for each arm
   are recorded as a comment on this item. The measured cause is stated
   explicitly (fallback probe vs process-lifetime accumulation); if the
   fallback is exonerated, the ACs below are re-scoped with the producer before
   implementation proceeds.
2. **SUPERSEDED — revoked by the producer re-scope of 2026-11-01 (see the Addendum below); evaluated against the re-scoped Option A intent (documentation-only), not the superseded literal text.** Original criterion: **Path does not change the probe source** (decided scope): a clip above
   `CAPTURE_PROBE_STREAM_THRESHOLD_BYTES` recorded with `--output` outside the
   repository root reports `probeSource: 'stream'`, and `probeSourceReason`
   no longer reports the in-page fallback for that case — asserted by a test
   that drives the source-selection/serving seam (no browser required).
3. **SUPERSEDED — revoked by the producer re-scope of 2026-11-01 (see the Addendum below); evaluated against the re-scoped Option A intent (documentation-only), not the superseded literal text.** Original criterion: **Any probe-serving route is narrow and capture-only**: a test asserts the
   route serves only the clip currently being probed (a request for any other
   path, including another file in the repo or an arbitrary filesystem path, is
   rejected) and that the route is registered only by the capture harness, not
   by `npm run dev` or a production build.
4. **SUPERSEDED — revoked by the producer re-scope of 2026-11-01 (see the Addendum below); evaluated against the re-scoped Option A intent (documentation-only), not the superseded literal text.** Original criterion: **Probe contract unchanged**: `durationSeconds`,
   `videoWidth`/`videoHeight`, `nonBlackFraction`, colour variety, `motion`,
   `audioPeak`, `audioRms`, `audioDecodeError`, `audioTrackCount` and
   `sampleProbes` keep their existing shape and semantics for both sources, and
   the additive `audioProbeBytes`/`audioProbeCapped`/`probeSource*` fields keep
   their meaning — the existing `scripts/capture-probe.test.ts` suite stays
   green without weakening an assertion.
5. **SUPERSEDED — revoked by the producer re-scope of 2026-11-01 (see the Addendum below); evaluated against the re-scoped Option A intent (documentation-only), not the superseded literal text.** Original criterion: **Budget holds for a supported output path** (decided scope): a > 32 MiB clip
   (or the 5-clip batch) recorded with `--output /tmp/…` reports
   `node.peakRssBytes` below 512 MiB, and the before/after figures are recorded
   on this item against the documented budget.
6. **SUPERSEDED — revoked by the producer re-scope of 2026-11-01 (see the Addendum below); evaluated against the re-scoped Option A intent (documentation-only), not the superseded literal text.** Original criterion: **A residual fallback is never silent** (Q3 = a): when a clip still falls
   back to the in-page probe, the run prints an actionable hint next to the
   existing `probeSourceReason` (that the streamed probe needs the output
   inside the repository root, and that the fallback costs the measured
   temporary RSS), and the clip is still recorded and probed — asserted by a
   test on the reporting seam.
7. **Documentation matches behaviour**:
   `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Probing long clips from the streamed file
   and §Long-run memory budget state which output paths keep the streamed
   probe and what the in-page fallback costs, using measured numbers with
   provenance; the reproduction commands that currently point at
   `--output /tmp/soak.webm` are corrected or explicitly annotated so a reader
   can reproduce the stated figure on the path the budget covers. Any
   user-visible capture behaviour change is reflected in `README.md`, and
   `src/captureStreamingDocs.test.ts` extends its guard to the new statements
   (without pinning host-specific measured values).
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, `README.md`, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependency.** The parent's recorded assumption stands: keep
  the in-page decode for small clips rather than adding `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` or
  any new package.
- **Do not raise the 512 MiB budget.** The docs call these caps overflow
  defences, not tuning knobs; the fix is to remove the cause, never to widen
  the number.
- **Never fail an already-recorded clip.** A probe that cannot load its source
  keeps the documented fallback and reports why (existing salvage contract),
  even after this change.
- **Capture tool stays loader-free.** `scripts/*.mjs` must keep running as plain
  ESM with node built-ins (types live in the sibling `.d.mts` files); no
  TypeScript loader may be required.
- **No gameplay/gym impact.** This is capture tooling; the gym↔game parity rule
  does not apply, and no `src/scenes/` behaviour may change.
- **No CI wiring.** Long-run soaks remain manual (parent AC4); the fix must not
  add a soak to any pipeline.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — misdiagnosis (highest).** If the 661 MiB peak is process-lifetime
  accumulation across five clips rather than the fallback probe, a fix aimed at
  the probe buys nothing. Mitigation: AC1 measures before changing code.
- **Risk — a file-serving route widens the attack surface.** A dev-server route
  serving arbitrary paths would expose the filesystem. Mitigation: tokenised,
  single-file, capture-harness-only registration, with AC3's negative tests.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Adjacent hardening (bounding the in-page decode,
  enforcing the budget at runtime, per-clip RSS attribution in diagnostics) is
  *not* in scope; file it as a separate item if it turns out to be required.
- **Risk — evidence rot.** The filed artefacts are gone, so the numbers in the
  original report cannot be re-checked without a fresh run; the re-measurement
  in AC1/AC5 is mandatory rather than a formality.
- **Assumption.** `--output /tmp/…` remains a supported invocation (it is
  documented in three places) rather than being deprecated in favour of an
  in-repo path. If the producer prefers deprecation, Option A absorbs it.
- **Assumption.** The probe must keep using the browser (Web Audio +
  `<video>`) rather than an out-of-browser analyser, per the existing design.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-probe.mjs` — `chooseProbeSource`, `buildProbeFileUrl` (the
  served-root restriction) and `probeRecordingInPage`: extend the serving
  decision so an outside-root clip can still be streamed.
- `scripts/capture-probe.d.mts` — types for any new serving options/route.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `stopRecordingAndProbe` (~L3052, the
  fallback seam) and the Vite server creation (~L2329) where a capture-only
  serving plugin would register.
- `scripts/capture-probe.test.ts` — extend the `buildProbeFileUrl` suite and
  add the outside-root → streamed-probe test (plus route-scope negatives).
- `vite/plugins/botTuningPlugin.ts`, `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`,
  `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — middleware precedents to copy the shape
  from (not to modify).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — §Probing long clips from the streamed file
  (~L733), §Long-run memory budget (~L770) and the `--output /tmp/soak.webm`
  reproduction commands (~L56, ~L798, ~L891).
- `src/captureStreamingDocs.test.ts` — docs guard to extend.
- `scripts/capture-diagnostics.mjs` — RSS sampling (`sampleRss`, heartbeat
  summary) if the measurement needs per-clip attribution.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE** (parent, completed) — capture crash on long full-run
  clips; defines the streaming/prefix budget design and the sanctioned
  size-threshold fallback.
- **AH-0MVNT28SJ008ZHDB** (completed) — implemented the streamed probe and
  `buildProbeFileUrl`'s served-root rule; the code this item extends.
- **AH-0MVNT2BBV008C4HT** (completed) — documented streaming, caps, partial
  output and the long-run budget (partial overlap: the doc to correct; it did
  not cover the outside-root path).
- **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (completed) — verification soak that surfaced this;
  its comment holds the 661.0 MiB / 408.9 MiB / 464.4 MiB figures.
- **AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ** (completed) — instrumentation that produced the RSS
  sampling used for the budget.
- **AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH** (completed) — neighbouring long-run memory work
  (run-end telemetry upload overflow); same class of "documented bound crossed".

## Duplicate-work check

Performed (`wl search` on "served repository root", "peak RSS", "in-page
fallback probe", "--output outside"). No completed item covers a `> 32 MiB` clip
written outside the served root blowing the `< 512 MiB` budget: the closest
items (AH-0MVNT2BBV008C4HT documentation, AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES verification)
overlap on *where the doc lives* but neither states or fixes the path
dependency, so this item proceeds rather than being closed as a duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

Intake round 1 was an unattended dispatch (no operator present), so the
questions were recorded as OPEN QUESTION and the item was flagged
`needsProducerReview`. Round 2: the producer answered all three; the accepted
answers are recorded below and the flag is cleared.

- **Q1 — Scope: document the path dependency, or make the streamed probe work
  for outputs outside the repo root?**
  Options: (A) documentation-only — state the served-root requirement, publish
  the fallback's measured RSS cost, and move the reproduction commands to an
  in-repo path; (B) make the streamed probe work for every supported output
  path via a capture-only route serving the clip being probed, plus docs;
  (C) B, but only if Q2 confirms the fallback is the cause.
  **Recommended:** C — the `< 512 MiB` budget is a documented contract and
  `--output /tmp/…` is one of the documented ways to reproduce it, so the
  budget should hold on every supported path; gating on Q2's measurement keeps
  the work pointed at the real cause.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30):** **C** — fix the serving seam, gated on
  the measurement. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions comment.

- **Q2 — Is the attribution correct, and may the measurement phase precede the
  fix?** The filed cause is an in-page `decodeAudioData` of the retained
  prefix, but that decode runs in the Chromium page, while the budget is
  measured from node's `process.memoryUsage().rss`; the 661.0 MiB figure is
  also a 5-clip batch outside the root versus a single 600 s clip inside it
  (longest single run in that batch: 464.4 MiB).
  Options: (A) measure first with a controlled A/B (same count/length inside vs
  outside the root, plus a single `> 32 MiB` clip to `/tmp`) and re-scope if
  the fallback is exonerated; (B) accept the filed attribution and go straight
  to the fix.
  **Recommended:** A — the current evidence varies two things at once (probe
  source *and* batch composition), so a fix built on it could miss.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30):** **A** — measure first with the controlled
  A/B, and re-scope if the fallback is exonerated.

- **Q3 — What should happen at capture time when an output path forces the
  in-page fallback?** Options: (a) warn with an actionable hint (`--output`
  should be inside the repo root, or the fallback costs ~X MiB) and continue;
  (b) fail fast with an actionable error *before* recording starts when the
  output path is outside the served root; (c) keep today's silent fallback,
  reported only in `probeSourceReason`.
  **Recommended:** (a) for Option A, and (a) retained as the residual path's
  behaviour under Option B — never fail an already-recorded clip, but never let
  a budget-crossing path stay silent either.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30):** **(a)** — warn with an actionable hint and
  continue; never fail an already-recorded clip.

## Original filed content (preserved for traceability)

### Observation

A 5-clip full-run soak (`--count 5 --max-duration 1800000 --diagnostics`,
output written to `/tmp/ah-soak/`) completed every clip, but the process node
RSS peaked at **661.0 MiB** (clip 4 start) — above the documented **< 512 MiB**
target. The peak is not recording growth: it is `peakRssBytes` at the *start*
of a clip, carried over from the **previous** clip's end-of-clip probe, and
every clip's end-of-recording RSS was 320–388 MiB.

Cause: clips 3 (34.9 MiB) and 5 (62.75 MiB) are above the 32 MiB in-page probe
threshold, but their files sat outside the served repository root
(`/tmp/ah-soak/…`), so the probe fell back to the **in-page Blob** path
(documented fallback, reported by `probeSourceReason`). That fallback decodes
up to the 32 MiB retained prefix with `decodeAudioData` in one shot, which
inflates node RSS by a few hundred MiB temporarily. A control run of the same
workload with the output inside the repo root (`capture-output/soak/`,
600 s, 48.43 MiB) used the **streamed** probe and peaked at only **408.9 MiB**.

### Why it matters

The < 512 MiB budget is documented for a full-cap run, and `--output /tmp/…`
is a supported, documented invocation. The *path*-based fallback (and its RSS
cost) is not covered by the parent's stated fallback rationale, which only
sanctions the in-page decode for clips *below* a size threshold.

### Acceptance criteria (as filed — superseded by §Acceptance criteria above; the either/or fork is resolved by Appendix Q1)

1. Document, in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory budget, that
   the streamed probe needs the output inside the served repository root and
   that the in-page fallback costs a temporary whole-prefix audio decode
   (with the measured 661 MiB batch peak vs 408.9 MiB streamed as the
   evidence), or
2. Make the streamed probe work for outputs outside the served root (e.g. a
   temporary route serving the partial file), restoring the < 512 MiB budget
   for every supported output path.
3. Re-run a > 32 MiB clip with `--output /tmp/…` and record the peak RSS
   against the budget.

### Evidence

Full numbers, per-clip diagnostics and logs: comment on
AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES; diagnostics artefacts under `/tmp/ah-soak/`
(`batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`) and
`capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVNT28SJ008ZHDB** – Probe long clips from the streamed file (contract preserved) (completed)
- **AH-0MVTEKPM6003R5NW** – Multi-scene capture breaks mid-sequence: __aiHellFade lost, recording salvaged (completed)
- **AH-0MVMIK8EM001JAYR** – Compiled videos cannot be fast forwarded (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absent, absorbs, ac1, ac3, ac4 (+422 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: 0mvnt25ji004ovkq, 0mvnt28sj008zhdb, 0mvnvgp55002g0kh, absent, ac1 (+414 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, absorbs, ac1, ac3, ac4 (+396 more)

## Addendum — AC1 outcome and producer re-scope (2026-11-01)

The AC1 controlled A/B (child **AH-0MVWAIHD5000I31Z**) **exonerated the in-page fallback**. Measured on unchanged `dev` (d4ace9550), same 420 s scripted workload, one clip per arm: in-root -> `stream`, whole-process VmHWM 782.4 MiB @ 3226 ms; out-of-root -> `in-page` fallback, VmHWM 783.5 MiB @ 3162 ms; in-root control 784.2 MiB @ 3259 ms. Every peak is at process startup (~3.2 s, Vite boot), before recording and ~475 s before the probe; the fallback costs ~+14 MiB during the probe window and ~+33 MiB after it, not the hundreds needed to explain 661 MiB. Full table, methodology and caveats are in this item's measurement comment.

**Producer decision (2026-11-01):** Q1 = **yes** — re-scope to the former Option A (documentation-only); Q2 = **fold the 512 MiB budget re-baseline into the re-scope**; Q3 = agent's call on child disposition.

**Re-scope applied:**

- Children 2–6 (serving seam, probe route, wiring, warning helper, separate budget verification) are **descoped and closed** with reasons; no serving or behaviour change ships.
- **AH-0MVWAIKSH009R6EH** (Update capture docs and docs guard) is the single remaining deliverable; its description now carries the re-scoped ACs, including the folded-in budget re-baseline.
- Acceptance criteria 2–6 above are **superseded** by the re-scope; AC7/AC8/AC9 (docs match behaviour, all related docs updated, full suite) remain and are restated in child AH-0MVWAIKSH009R6EH.
- The `< 512 MiB` budget is **not** raised. The re-baseline records that on the 2026-11-01 host the whole-process peak (~767–784 MiB) is at Vite boot and is path-independent, so the documented budget is a recording-window figure and needs a fresh idle-host baseline.

**Note on evidence:** the raw `/tmp/ab` measurement artefacts were reaped by host temp cleanup after the run; the figures are preserved in this item's measurement comment and the child session log, and are cited from there.

The Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA) delivers the weapon's baked launch and hit `playWeaponFireSound`/`impactFx` cues only. It deliberately does not add a `muzzleFlash` VFX spec, because the tracer's in-flight identity (`tracer`, length 8, rim 0xe0f0ff, trail 4.5, size 1.15, sky blue 0x66aaff) is already strong and the parent item was scoped to audio.

Remaining gap: the Railgun is one of the five net-new unlock-pool weapons (AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW) that never received the per-weapon feel package. It has no `muzzleFlash` metadata, so `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` spawns no launch flash (unlike the Wave Laser's wide 12 px neon burst or the Arc's electric purple pop).

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want a short heavy sky-blue launch flash at the hull when the Railgun fires (once per four beats), so the shot's weight reads visually as well as audibly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `railgun` catalogue entry declares `muzzleFlash` (sky-blue `BULLET_COLORS.railgun` family, radius/duration sized between the Cannon's 7 px/0.12 s and the Wave Laser's 12 px/0.15 s flare, befitting a heavy single shot).
- The flash is spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, so `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling` show it identically with no per-scene code.
- `resolveWeaponDefinition` carries the new metadata through levelling unchanged (test).
- Docs (GDD §4.4 Railgun row, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` notes if applicable) mention the launch flash; no balance/behaviour change.
- Full project test suite passes, including the muzzle-flash and gym-parity guards.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

data.description:
Wave laser should be changed to be a single red beam that is fired. It has a very long range and does 1 damage to anything it intercepts with. When it intercepts it stops at that point. If no intercept it will travel for a full screen width, wrapping at the edges. It is visible for 0.3s and has a sci-fi laser SFX.

## User story

As the player, when the Wave Laser is active my ship fires a **single red beam** along its heading. The beam reaches right across the screen, deals **1 damage to the first enemy it touches** and stops there; if it touches nothing it crosses a **full screen width** (wrapping at the arena edges), it stays **visible for 0.3 s**, and it fires with a **sci-fi laser SFX**.

## Current behaviour (as shipped, for contrast)

- `wave_laser` is a slow travelling neon-blue bolt: `BULLET_SPEED` 350 px/s × `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME.wave_laser` 1.0 s ≈ 350 px range, `'line'` shape with a white rim, thickness 3, length 7 (AH-0MV822ACO007CEZF).
- It carries a **damage budget** (`maxHitPoints: 2`) and **passes through** the enemies it destroys, spending the remaining budget on the ships behind them (R-Type homage; AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92, AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S).
- The budget seam lives in `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` / `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` and is shared by the game and every gym; the Railgun is the only other budget weapon (base 5).
- The fire cue `playWaveLaserFireSound` → `aihell-wave-laser-fire` is already wired through `playWeaponFireSound` (a ~0.1 s high-energy square beam crack).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Single red beam.** A wave-laser shot renders as exactly one red beam (one `'line'`-shape bolt per shot: no fan, no pair); the catalogue colour and the wave-laser icon are red, and the identity stays distinguishable from the Heavy Slug's deep red (see Assumption A5).
- AC2 — **1 damage, stops at the first intercept.** The beam's ray resolves exactly 1 damage to the first enemy (or boss) it intersects and stops at that intersection; no second enemy takes damage from the same shot and no enemy is passed through (see Open Question Q1 → answer B: instant hitscan ray).
- AC3 — **Full-screen extent with no intercept.** With nothing in its path the beam's ray extends at least a full screen width (`GAME_WIDTH` = 960 px), wrapping at the arena edges — a ray fired near the right edge continues from the left and keeps extending for the remainder of its width budget.
- AC4 — **0.3 s visibility.** The beam is rendered for 0.3 s from launch and removed when that elapses; no beam body, trail or flash from the shot persists beyond 0.3 s.
- AC5 — **Sci-fi laser SFX.** Launch plays a sci-fi laser fire cue through the shared `playWeaponFireSound` dispatcher, backed by a baked ToneForge recipe with the manifest, sfx asset, checksums and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` all regenerated; it honours the existing voice-limit/gating rules and the connect keeps its own baked impact cue.
- AC6 — **Unchanged cadence and drop.** The fire cadence stays 1 shot per beat (750 ms at the default 80 BPM) on the shared beat grid, and the pickup remains a timed 10 s drop with the same hangar unlock entry (`wave_laser`, 120 minerals / 1 core). *(Assumption A4 — see Open Question Q2.)*
- AC7 — **Fixed damage at every level.** The 1-damage/stop-at-first-intercept rule holds at every weapon level: the level curve no longer grants the wave laser a growing damage budget (`maxHitPoints`), and its level-up variables keep a monotonic, documented effect instead. *(Assumption A6 — see Open Question Q3.)*
- AC8 — **Game↔gym parity.** The shipped behaviour runs through the shared core in `src/scenes/core/` so `PlayScene` and `GymWeapons` behave identically; any retained divergence is recorded in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
- AC9 — **Docs and roster consistency.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 P3, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` §1 and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` describe the new single-hit, screen-spanning beam, and no docs/roster assertion still expects piercing or pass-through for the wave laser (e.g. the `weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts` phrase "Long horizontal beam with pass-through chevrons").
- AC10 — **Tests.** Unit tests cover: 1 damage at the first intersection (two enemies in a line → only the first is damaged); an unobstructed ray spanning at least `GAME_WIDTH`; the edge wrap (ray fired near each edge); the beam colour/shape identity; and the fire-cue dispatch. The changed-scope and full suites pass.
- AC11 — **Dedicated shared ray seam, projectiles untouched.** The wave laser resolves through a dedicated raycast seam in `src/scenes/core/` shared by `PlayScene` and the gyms; the travelling-bullet flight/collision path is unchanged for every other weapon (no per-weapon speed seam, no tunnelling risk, no regression in existing bullet tests).

**Key Files:**

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `wave_laser` definition: red colour, single-beam visual, 0.3 s lifetime, damage-budget retirement, optional per-weapon speed.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `GAME_WIDTH` (960) and `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` (350), the basis for the full-width range.
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — `'line'` beam drawing, rim, thickness and trail.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — lifetime, four-edge wrap and fast-bullet advance.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared auto-fire spawn path (bullet-speed seam, muzzle flash).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared collision/damage path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`).
- `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` — new pure ray helper (wrapped-width march, nearest enemy intersection, endpoint) shared by the game and the gyms.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — wave-laser level variables and the `maxHitPoints` growth rule.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWaveLaserFireSound` / `playWeaponFireSound` dispatch.
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-wave-laser-fire.yaml` — the baked fire-cue recipe to refresh.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — cue manifest entry (seed + recipe) for the regenerated asset.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — parity gym that exercises the wave laser.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — wave-laser icon colour/shape.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 weapon table (P3 Wave Laser).
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — §1 adaptation and documented divergence.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — cue description table.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — parity matrix (update only if a divergence is retained).

## Implementation sketch

*Test-first: each step below lands its failing test before the production change (project policy), and the whole change is one vertical slice — definition, shared core, audio, gym parity, docs and tests in a single delivery — so no child items are needed.*

*Design settled by the producer answers: Q1 = **B (instant hitscan ray, rendered 0.3 s)**, Q2 = **A (1 shot per beat)**, Q3 = **A (damage fixed at 1 at every level)**.*

1. **Definition (`src/utils/weapons.ts`).** Make `BULLET_COLORS.wave_laser` red; keep `offsets: [0]` and the 1/beat cadence; remove `maxHitPoints` (the beam no longer carries a damage budget) and add the hit-resolution marker the shared ray seam dispatches on (e.g. a `hitscan` descriptor on the definition), plus `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME`-equivalent beam duration of 0.3 s for the visual.
2. **Shared ray seam (`src/scenes/core/`).** A new pure, unit-testable raycast helper (geometry segment vs circle, plus the wrapped-width march: continue the ray from the opposite screen edge when it crosses a boundary) consumed by the shared fire path in `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`. It finds the nearest intersection along the (possibly wrapped) ray, deals exactly 1 damage to that enemy via the existing damage/finalise seams (`damageEnemyWithBullet` + `onEnemyDestroyed`), and reports the endpoint for the visual. `GymWeapons` and `PlayScene` inherit it, so parity is by construction (AC8, AC11).
3. **Beam visual (`src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` + a beam object).** Draw the resolved ray from the muzzle to the endpoint as a single red beam (straight segment, or two segments when it wraps an edge), held for 0.3 s and then destroyed — with the existing muzzle flash at launch and the existing wave-laser impact cue/flash at the intercept point. The travelling-bullet path stays untouched for every other weapon.
4. **Wrap and extent tests.** Prove the ray extends at least `GAME_WIDTH` (960 px) unobstructed, that a wrap continues from the opposite edge with the remaining width budget, and that a wrapped ray still hits the first enemy it meets (e.g. a target behind the ship when the ray wraps the far edge).
5. **Level curve.** Retire the `maxHitPoints` growth for `wave_laser` (`resolveWeaponAtLevel`/`resolveWeaponDefinition` only apply it to weapons whose base declares a budget) and document which variables now carry its upgrade; update the `weaponLevels` tests that assert a ~7 saturation.
6. **Audio.** Refresh the baked cue (`aihell-wave-laser-fire`) with a sci-fi laser recipe, regenerate the manifest/sfx asset/checksums, and update `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` plus the `src/audio/effects.test.ts` expectations; keep the baked impact cue.
7. **Parity.** `GymWeapons` inherits the behaviour through the shared core — extend its tests (inert practice targets demonstrate the stop-at-first-intercept rule) and update `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` only if a divergence is retained.
8. **Docs and rosters.** Update GDD §4.4 P3 (and the icon/visual phrase), the research doc's adaptation/divergence text, and the roster/visual docs assertions so nothing still claims piercing.

## Assumptions (producer to confirm)

- **A1:** "1 damage" means one hit point per shot — an enemy with more HP survives and the beam still stops.
- **A2:** "Is visible for 0.3 s" is the beam's render duration (the hit resolves instantly at launch), not a travel time.
- **A3:** "Full screen width" means at least `GAME_WIDTH` (960 px) of ray extent.
- **A4:** The 1/beat cadence and the timed 10 s drop are unchanged. *(Confirmed by the producer: Q2 = A.)*
- **A5:** "Red" is pure red (~`0xff0000`), distinct from the Heavy Slug's deep red `0xff2222` by hue and by shape.
- **A6:** Level-ups must not break the 1-damage rule, so the damage budget is retired for this weapon. *(Confirmed by the producer: Q3 = A.)*
- **A7:** The beam is hitscan, so there is no travelling bolt: the 0.3 s is the visible beam column from the muzzle to its endpoint. *(Confirmed by the producer: Q1 = B.)*

## Open Questions

- **RESOLVED Q1 (beam model)** — producer answer: **B, instant hitscan ray rendered for 0.3 s** (from the ship to the first intercept, or a wrapped full-width extent). This replaces the travelling projectile; the collision work becomes a shared raycast seam (AC2/AC3/AC11) rather than a per-weapon speed seam, and there is no tunnelling risk.
- **RESOLVED Q2 (cadence)** — producer answer: **A, keep 1 shot per beat** (750 ms at 80 BPM), so a 0.3 s beam never overlaps the next shot.
- **RESOLVED Q3 (level scaling)** — producer answer: **A, damage stays 1 at every level** and the wave laser's upgrades move to beam width/visual size; its `maxHitPoints` damage budget is retired (the Railgun keeps the budget seam).

No open questions remain for planning; implementation can start once the work item is resumed.

## Related work and duplicate check

- **Duplicate check performed** — no existing item covers this scope. `wl search "wave laser"` found:
  - AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92 "R-Type piercing wave laser" (completed) and AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S "Wave Laser should have limited hit power" (completed) — they *built* the pierced/budget behaviour this item now replaces; keep them as history, not duplicates.
  - AH-0MV822ACO007CEZF "Wave Laser projectile visuals & feel" (completed) — the current visual/feel package being reworked.
  - AH-0MV1EDVNF004MTYN "Wave laser audio fire/pickup cues and leveling-gym round-robin" (open, low) — partially overlaps AC5, but its premise ("the wave laser currently fires silently") is stale; it remains open for the pickup cue and leveling-gym round-robin.
  - AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE "Variery in weapon graphics" (completed) — the per-weapon visual roster context.
- Reference design docs: `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` §1 (R-Type wave laser), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (P3 Wave Laser), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (parity matrix).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-31T10:07:52Z — Plan session (auto-complete path: no children needed, single-weapon vertical slice). Added the user story, current-behaviour contrast, AC1–AC10, Key Files, implementation sketch, assumptions A1–A6, Open Questions Q1–Q3 and the duplicate-check record. No child items created; AC coverage review verified the item is its own delivery slice.
- 2026-10-31T11:53:19Z — Producer answered the three questions in-session (Q1 = B hitscan ray, Q2 = A 1/beat, Q3 = A fixed 1 damage). Re-claimed the item, recorded the answers in the Appendix, reworded AC2/AC3/AC4 and added AC11 for the dedicated shared ray seam, replaced the projectile speed/tunnelling steps in the implementation sketch with the shared raycast seam, added `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` to Key Files, and cleared needs-producer-review.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31T11:53:19Z (via the plan session, after the handoff comment on this work item).

- **Q1 — Beam model: travelling projectile or instant hitscan ray?**
  - Q as asked: "Q1 — beam model (blocks the collision design in AC2/AC3/AC4). Option A: keep a travelling projectile — one red beam travelling at >= 3200 px/s so 0.3 s covers the 960 px screen width — reusing the existing four-edge wrap and shared collision path. Option B: an instant hitscan ray drawn from the ship to the first intercept (or a wrapped full-width span) and rendered for 0.3 s."
  - Answer (producer): **B — instant hitscan ray rendered for 0.3 s.** Final: B.
  - Effect on the plan: the collision work is a new dedicated shared raycast seam (`src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` + the shared fire path) instead of a per-weapon bullet speed seam; there is no tunnelling risk and no change to the travelling-bullet path. AC2/AC3/AC4 reworded for a ray; AC11 added for the seam. Evidence for the decision context: `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` (wrap + lifetime), `src/utils/weapons.ts` (`BULLET_SPEED` 350, `GAME_WIDTH` 960 in `src/core/constants.ts`), `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`).

- **Q2 — Fire cadence: keep 1 shot per beat or speed it up?**
  - Q as asked: "Q2 — fire cadence (affects AC6). Option A: keep 1 shot per beat (750 ms at 80 BPM) so a 0.3 s beam never overlaps the next shot. Option B: speed the cadence up (e.g. 2/beat = 375 ms)."
  - Answer (producer): **A — keep 1 shot per beat.** Final: A.
  - Effect on the plan: AC6 unchanged in substance and now confirmed; `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS.wave_laser` stays `1` (the beat-grid invariant `isOnBeatGrid` is untouched).

- **Q3 — Level scaling: fixed 1 damage or a growing piercing budget?**
  - Q as asked: "Q3 — level scaling (affects AC7). Option A: damage stays 1 at every level and the wave laser's upgrades move to beam width/visual size, retiring its maxHitPoints damage budget (the Railgun keeps the budget seam). Option B: the budget keeps growing with level so a high-level beam pierces more enemies."
  - Answer (producer): **A — damage stays 1 at every level.** Final: A.
  - Effect on the plan: AC7 confirmed; `maxHitPoints` is removed from the `wave_laser` definition and the `weaponLevels` tests that assert a ~7 saturation for `wave_laser` are replaced with tests for the retained width/visual variables. The railgun's budget behaviour is unchanged.

No further questions outstanding.
