Discovered-from: AH-0MVUXH35J002WSAB (hold-full choice charge grant).

## Problem statement

A run checkpoint persists a consumable's **permanent level** but not its
**charge pool** or its in-flight recharge timers. `PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint`
replays `grantPermanentPowerUp` once per persisted level, and an owned
consumable is persisted at level 1 (a hold-full grant never levels it), so a
resumed run can only ever hold one charge and loses every spent-charge
regeneration clock. A run that banked three Shield charges and then resumed
silently loses two of them.

## Users (user stories)

- **As an arcade player** resuming from the last mini-boss checkpoint, I want
  the consumable charges I earned (and the recharge timers already running) to
  be exactly as I left them, so that Continue does not punish me for stopping.
- **As a player with a partially spent pool**, I want a charge that was
  mid-regeneration to keep regenerating on resume, so that the pool behaves as
  one continuous resource across the save.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the restored pool to flow through the one shared
  `PowerUpLevelStore` seam, so the checkpoint can never become a second
  charge counter that drifts from live play.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Save captures pools and timers.** A checkpoint written at a
  mini-boss defeat records, for each owned consumable (`shield`, `thorns`,
  `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `force_field`, `mystery_ufo`), its current charge
  count and the remaining seconds of every in-flight recharge timer.
- **AC2 — Resume restores them through the shared store seam.** A resumed run
  restores the pools and timers through `PowerUpLevelStore` (no second counter,
  no scene-local shadow state), and the resumed pool equals the saved pool
  exactly — including a pool of three charges and two partially elapsed
  recharge timers.
- **AC3 — Legacy payloads still resume.** A checkpoint payload with no charge
  fields loads and resumes exactly as today: the permanent-grant replay leaves
  each owned consumable with its single granted charge and no timers. The
  checkpoint schema version is **not** bumped (the new field is additive and
  optional), because the version gate rejects any payload stamped with another
  version.
- **AC4 — Tests pin both the round trip and the legacy fallback.** Unit tests
  cover the store snapshot/restore seam, the checkpoint round trip, defensive
  parsing, the slot-gate interaction and the legacy (no charge fields) resume
  path; the PlayScene tests cover save-side capture and resume-side restoration
  end to end.
- **AC5 — Defensive parsing and slot gate.** Malformed pool entries (unknown
  or non-consumable ids, negative/non-finite charges, non-finite timers, an
  absent array) are dropped or clamped rather than throwing, and a kind dropped
  by `capCheckpointLoadout`'s six-slot gate loses its charge pool too, so a
  resumed run can never hold charges for a kind it does not own.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.6 (the
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` storage row) and the `checkpointStore` module/version
  comment describe the persisted pool and the legacy fallback; the gym-parity
  note explains why no gym needs a change.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
  changes.

## Constraints

- **No schema-version bump.** `parseCheckpoint` rejects any payload whose
  `version` is not exactly `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` (3). AC3 requires legacy v3
  payloads to keep resuming, so the new field is optional and additive; a bump
  would be a breaking change and is explicitly out of scope.
- **One source of truth.** The pool and timers live in `PowerUpLevelStore`;
  the checkpoint only serialises and rehydrates them. The save path must read
  the same store instance the HUD and effect path read (`Player.getPowerUpLevelStore()`
  / `EffectsRegistry.levelStore()`), not `PowerUpLevelStore` internals.
- **Restore ordering.** Permanent grants are replayed first (that is what marks
  a consumable owned and sets its level-derived cap/interval), then the saved
  pool and timers are re-applied authoritatively, then lives — so the replay's
  single per-level grant can never leak into the saved pool.
- **Parity.** No gym implements checkpoint resume, so no gym scene needs a
  counterpart; the shared store API is consumed by the game and the gyms alike.
  Record this in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` reasoning if the matrix enumerates resume
  seams.
- **Scope guard.** Migrating consumables onto the charge pool for field
  pickups, HUD countdowns and effect-path convergence belong to the parent epic
  (AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW) and its follow-ups; this item only adds persistence.

## Existing state

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — `Checkpoint` v3 persists `weaponLevels` and
  `powerUpLevels` only; `toLevelList` is the defensive list parser;
  `capCheckpointLoadout` is the save-side six-slot gate.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_saveCheckpoint` builds the payload from
  `player.getPowerUpLevels()`; `_restoreCheckpoint` replays
  `grantPermanentWeapon` / `grantPermanentPowerUp` once per persisted level.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore` already owns
  `_charges` and `_rechargeTimers` with `consumableCharges`,
  `consumableChargeCap`, `consumableRechargeTime`,
  `consumableRechargeRemaining` (minimum timer only), `grantConsumableCharge`,
  `consumeConsumableCharge` and `tickRecharge`. It exposes **no** per-kind
  snapshot of all timers and **no** restore/set entry point.
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` — `grantPermanentPowerUp` is the single
  hold-full grant seam; for a consumable `collect(id, true)` adds exactly one
  charge and never raises the level.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.6 storage table row and §4.4.3 describe
  the checkpoint payload and the consumable charge model.

## Desired change

1. Add a small, pure `PowerUpLevelStore` snapshot/restore seam (e.g.
   `snapshotConsumablePools()` returning `{ id, charges, rechargeTimers }[]` and
   `restoreConsumablePools(entries)`) so a caller can read every in-flight timer
   and rehydrate it without touching private maps.
2. Extend `Checkpoint` with an optional `consumablePools` field (array of
   `{ id, charges, rechargeTimers }`), parsed defensively and dropped from
   payloads for any kind the six-slot gate removes; keep `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`
   at 3 and document the field as additive.
3. `PlayScene._saveCheckpoint` reads the pool snapshot from the player's single
   `PowerUpLevelStore`; `_restoreCheckpoint` re-applies it **after** the
   permanent-grant replay and before the lives restore.
4. Update the checkpoint documentation (§6.6 row, module/version comment) and
   add the tests named in AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — new optional `consumablePools` field, defensive parser, slot-gate interaction, version-comment update
- `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts` — round-trip, defensive-parse, legacy-fallback and slot-gate tests
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `snapshotConsumablePools` / `restoreConsumablePools` (or equivalent) on `PowerUpLevelStore`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — snapshot/restore seam tests, including partially elapsed timers
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_saveCheckpoint` capture and `_restoreCheckpoint` restore ordering
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — end-to-end save capture and resume restoration
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.6 `ai_hell_checkpoint` row and §4.4.3 charge-model note

## Related work

### Automated find-related report

Related work items:

- **AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2** – Shared consumable charge pool in PowerUpLevelStore (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** – Registry one-event consumption and regeneration accessors (completed)
- **AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT** – Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore (completed)

Repository file matches:

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: checkpoint, charge, consumable, persisted
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, checkpoint, charge
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: checkpoint, charge

### Related work items (context)

- **AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2** — Shared consumable charge pool in `PowerUpLevelStore`
  (completed): the pool, timers, ownership flag and `tickRecharge` this item
  persists.
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** — Registry one-event consumption and regeneration
  accessors (completed): the effect-path accessors the resumed state feeds.
- **AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT** — Per-charge recharge engine in `PowerUpLevelStore`
  (completed): the per-charge timer semantics that must round-trip.
- **AH-0MVUXH35J002WSAB** — Hold-full choice charge grant (open, discovered-from
  source): owns the grant that makes a pool larger than one possible.
- **AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW** — Consumable charge pool epic (open): parent design
  decision that permanence is a regenerating charge pool, so pool contents are
  earned run state.
- **AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51** / **AH-0MVT1DYO5004UC4P** / **AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP**
  (completed) — the checkpoint save/resume, schema-v2 capacity and
  resumed-HUD seams this change extends.
- **AH-0MVT1DZRG000Q1US** (completed) — precedent for "apply capacity first,
  then clamp" restore ordering.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — restore ordering leak.** Replaying the permanent grant adds one
  charge; restoring the pool afterwards is what makes the pool authoritative.
  Mitigation: an explicit test asserting a saved pool of 0 charges survives a
  resume of an owned kind (the replay's charge must not reappear).
- **Risk — over-cap pool on resume.** A hand-edited payload could name more
  charges than the level-derived cap. Mitigation: clamp on restore to
  `consumableChargeCap` and drop non-consumable ids during parse; legitimate
  saves always fit, so AC2's "matches exactly" still holds.
- **Risk — second counter.** Mitigation: the snapshot/restore seam lives on
  `PowerUpLevelStore`; the checkpoint never reads or writes `_charges` /
  `_rechargeTimers` directly.
- **Assumption A1 —** timer values are persisted as **remaining seconds**
  (not absolute timestamps), so a resume continues each charge's countdown
  where it stopped; wall-clock time spent away from the game does not
  regenerate charges.
- **Assumption A2 —** ownership itself needs no new field: it is already
  re-derived from the replayed permanent-grant snapshot (`getLevels()` reports
  an owned consumable at level 1).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Field-pickup charge conversion, HUD countdowns and
  effect-path convergence are parent-epic work; extra opportunities are
  recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No producer questions were required: the item's acceptance criteria resolve the
two design forks the repo search surfaced.

- **Q: Should the checkpoint schema version be bumped for the new pool fields?**
  — Answer (repository evidence, AC3): **no**. `parseCheckpoint` rejects every
  payload whose `version !== CHECKPOINT_VERSION`, and AC3 requires legacy
  payloads to keep resuming, so the field is additive and optional. Evidence:
  `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` version gate; `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts`
  "a stale pre-wheel checkpoint version is rejected cleanly".
- **Q: Does any gym implement checkpoint resume, requiring a parity change?** —
  Answer (repository evidence): **no**. `PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint`'s doc
  comment records that no gym implements checkpoint resume, so only the shared
  `PowerUpLevelStore` seam is touched. Evidence:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_restoreCheckpoint` documentation; AGENTS.md
  gym↔game parity rules.
- **Q: Where do the timer values come from, given the store exposes only a
  minimum?** — Answer (repository evidence): the store keeps all per-charge
  timers in `_rechargeTimers` but only surfaces `consumableRechargeRemaining`
  (the minimum), so the change adds a snapshot/restore accessor pair rather
  than a second store. Evidence: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
  (`consumableRechargeRemaining`, `tickRecharge`, `_advanceRechargeTimers`).

User story
As a player I want each collected and upgraded weapon to fire on its own deterministic Euclidean rhythm, so that the superposition of all active weapons forms an emergent, evolving groove, and I want bullet visuals and fire sound to stay exactly in sync.

Design decisions (agreed with producer)
1. The Euclidean pattern is the cadence itself, not a decoration. patternFor(weaponId, level) is a pure, deterministic function returning { k, n, rotation, stepMs }. Same weapon + same level => same rhythm => same sound (consistency).
2. VFX/SFX sync by construction: the fire event is the onset; bullets, muzzle flash and fire cue dispatch on the same frame. No decoupled audio schedule.
3. Irregularity is the feature: gaps within a pattern are uneven (e.g. E(5,8) has 1- and 2-step gaps). Weapons are not required to fire on a regular beat.
4. Upgrades morph the pattern: the fire-rate upgrade walks a (k, n, rotation) ladder so the rhythm can change shape (density and/or phase), not merely speed up. Morphs land on the next bar downbeat (bar-boundary morph rule).
5. Grid: patterns live on the shared 16th-note lattice at 80 BPM (187.5 ms steps); one bar = 4 beats = 16 steps. Bar-aligned n in v1 (n such as 8 or 16, i.e. divisors of the bar); accidental polymeter (n = 3 or 5 lanes) deferred. The lattice is the scheduling solvent, not a metronome: onset sets are irregular within it.
6. Consistency: one fire cue per weapon (already true); the only thing that varies is when, deterministically per (weapon, level). No per-tick voice-flavour roulette.
7. Explosions unchanged: keep the shipped snap-to-next-16th explosion accent (setExplosionBeatClock) and its per-tick cap. Weapon-kill impacts are off-grid by construction (fire time + flight time), so the musical offset is deliberate; fire-time events (onFire/onRandom AOE such as nova, arc, mortar) already detonate on-lattice with zero delay. Do NOT remove or retime the explosion accent.
8. Determinism and replay: patterns are pure functions of (weapon, level) plus game time, with no RNG and no wall-clock reads, so seeded replay is unaffected.
9. Gym parity: all changes live in shared code (beat/euclid module, Player.tryFire, CombatCoreScene._autoFire); a new Rhythm gym auditions patterns; a GYM_PARITY.md row is added.

Acceptance criteria
- Each weapon fires only on onset ticks of its deterministic pattern; every shot time is provably an exact lattice tick.
- Same input schedule produces byte-identical shot sequences (determinism pinned by test).
- Fire VFX and fire SFX dispatch on the same frame as the fire event.
- Fire-rate upgrades keep onsets-per-minute monotonic non-decreasing in level and may change (k, n, rotation).
- Pattern changes take effect only on a bar downbeat.
- Explosion snap-to-16th behaviour is preserved unchanged (regression-guarded).
- A Rhythm gym demonstrates slow + medium + fast superposition and has a parity row.

References
src/utils/beat.ts (grid math), src/utils/weapons.ts (subdivisions, WeaponId), src/utils/weaponLevels.ts (quantiseSubdivision, fireRate curve), src/entities/Player.ts (tryFire), src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts (_autoFire), src/audio/effects.ts (explosion accent), docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md (tempo zones and fire grid), docs/GYM_PARITY.md.

Children: pure Euclidean pattern module; fire-scheduler refactor; upgrade (k, n, rotation) ladder; Rhythm gym + parity row.

Goal
Implement the pure Euclidean pattern module (sibling of src/utils/beat.ts, e.g. src/utils/euclid.ts) as the foundation for the epic AH-0MVYA1JFK003RLAW.

Scope
- euclidPattern(k, n, rotation): returns the maximally-even onset set of k onsets over n steps (Bjorklund/Euclidean), rotation applied mod n. Pure, no RNG, no wall clock.
- Grid helpers mirroring the beat.ts API: stepIndexAt(time, stepMs, anchor), isOnset(time, pattern, stepMs, anchor), nextOnsetTick(pattern step grid, time, anchor), nextOnsetDelayMs(...) for scheduling.
- stepMs comes from the existing beatSubdivisionMs API so the lattice stays the shared 16th-note grid at 80 BPM.

Explicitly out of scope
- No weapon/gameplay/audio coupling. No Player/scene changes. No ladder design (child AH-0MVYA1JFK003RLAW-C3).

Acceptance criteria (tests, hermetic)
- Known canonical patterns: E(3,8) = x..x..x., E(5,8) = x.xx.x.x, E(2,5) = x.x.. (up to documented rotation).
- Maximal-evenness property: cyclic gaps are only floor(n/k) or ceil(n/k).
- Complement symmetry: non-onset set of E(k,n) equals E(n-k,n) up to rotation.
- Rotation equivalence: rotating onsets by r yields the same rhythm class, and rotation 0 roots at step 0.
- Edge cases: k = 0 (empty), k = n (all onsets), k > n clamps to n, n = 1.
- Determinism: same inputs always produce identical output; no Date/Math.random; step-index math only.
- Grid alignment: every returned time matches an exact lattice tick.

Design and implement the per-weapon upgrade ladder: how fire-rate upgrades move each weapon through (k, n, rotation) pattern states so onsets-per-minute stay monotonic while the rhythm can change shape (epic AH-0MVYA1JFK003RLAW).

Scope

Degenerate straight patterns (E(n,n) at a subdivision) must resolve exactly as today's quantiseSubdivision does, so legacy cadences are the all-onsets subset.
- rotation as an explicit morph lever: a level may change phase at identical density (e.g. two medium weapons sharing k=9 differing only by rotation).
- Example ledger to document: cannon E(8,16) -> E(10,16) -> E(13,16) -> E(16,16) then bar-halving E(8,8) at 8th-note steps (shape change, not just faster). Slow weapons stay sparse-irregular (e.g. E(3,16), E(2,16)), not whole-beat multiples.
- Monotonic rule re-asserted in onsets-per-minute: effective density non-decreasing in level for every weapon.
- The 6-weapon 16-step superposition example (heavy_slug E(3,16), railgun E(2,16), cannon E(9,16), arc E(9,16 rot 4), rapid E(13,16), shard_swarm E(10,16)) is the canonical fixture; verify it still totals 46 onsets/bar until ladder values are tuned.

Explicitly out of scope
- Fire scheduling mechanics (child C2 consumes this). The Rhythm gym (child C4).

Acceptance criteria
- onsets-per-minute monotonic non-decreasing in level across the whole weapon catalogue.
- quantiseEuclidean matches quantiseSubdivision for all-straight patterns.
- Ladder values are documented (weaponLevelingDocs / BALANCING.md style) and machine-verifiable.
- Hybrid tests: existing weaponLevels monotonicity tests extended to density space.
- Rotation morphs change phase without changing density, pinned by test.

# Upgrade count off-by-one: HUD label and upgrade screen show 5 when the player has 6 upgrades

**Headline:** Mid-run the player counts **six** upgrade rows in the HUD list, but the HUD `Loadout n/6` budget read-out shows **5/6** and the hold-full choice overlay's `YOUR UPGRADES` panel lists **five** owned items. Establish from a recording whether the sixth row is a slot-counted kind the model genuinely misses (an under-count bug) or a non-slot row (exempt `always available` / charge-pool `charges only`) that the player reads as an upgrade, then make the label, the HUD rows and the upgrade panel tell the same story.

## Problem statement

The report (operator, recent playtest): "the label mid-run said that we only had 5/6 upgrades, but we had 6. When I went into the upgrade screen it showed 5 not 6. Looks like we have an off by one error somewhere." Both the label (`resolvePlayerSlotState(...).used`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`) and the upgrade panel (`buildOwnedLoadout`, `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts`) are derived from the shared slot model, so a genuine "5 vs 6" can only mean **either** the model under-counts a kind it should hold (any acquisition path feeding the snapshots is missing something), **or** one of the six visible HUD rows is a non-slot row that neither surface counts by design (exempt `extra_life`/`mystery_ufo`, or a Phase Shift/Teleport charge pool left after a temporary window expired). The parent RCA (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX) established these row classes exist.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want the upgrade count, the upgrade list and the upgrade screen to agree with what my ship actually carries, so I can trust the loadout read-out mid-run."
- **Developer/maintainer** — "As a developer, I want one slot model and one display derived from it with no second counter, so a label can never disagree with the row list by one again."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction and characterisation.** A recorded fresh-run session (`npm run record`, operator-supplied path) or an equivalent scene test shows six upgrade rows in the HUD while `Loadout n/6` reads 5/6 and the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel lists five; each of the six rows is classified as slot-counted or non-slot (exempt entry / residual charge pool), and the classification is recorded as a comment on this item with the evidence path.
2. **No slot model under-count.** Every slot-counted kind held by the player (permanent or temporary) is present in `resolveSlotState(...).heldIds` and counted in `used`; any acquisition surface that grants a kind without the snapshots reflecting it (capture/setup, checkpoint resume, charge-grant reward, mini-boss unlock) is gated or fixed through the shared helper. Regression test: for a mixed permanent + temporary loadout, `resolveSlotState(...).used` equals the true held count and a seventh kind can never be dropped from the count.
3. **The displayed loadout agrees with the model.** For the reported scenario the HUD's slot-counted rows equal `resolvePlayerSlotState(...).used`, the `Loadout n/6` label equals `used/cap`, the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel's permanent rows equal the model's permanent held kinds, and a non-slot row is visibly distinguished (an `always available` / `charges only` marker, grouping, or label) so it cannot be mistaken for an upgrade. Asserted by HUD and overlay tests over a loadout that includes an exempt entry and a residual charge pool.
4. **Regression guard.** The reported scenario (replayed recording or fixture) no longer shows a count that disagrees with the model; if a genuine under-count was found, the failing surface is covered by a test that fails on the pre-fix code.
5. **Documentation and suite.** `docs/BALANCING.md` "The six loadout slots", GDD §4.4 and any HUD/overlay docs are updated to state how the label, rows and `YOUR UPGRADES` panel present occupancy and non-slot rows; all related documentation is updated, including code comments, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One rule, one implementation.** The fix belongs in `src/powerups/slots.ts` and its shared consumers (`HUD`, `ownedLoadout`, `MineralChoiceScene`, shared scene layer) — no per-scene or per-gym copy (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Keep the producer decisions.** Do not weaken Q4a (temporary pickups hold a slot), Q5b (blocked pickups stay on the field with the blocked cue), Q6a (the choice offers only what is in the slots) or Q7a (exempt entries never count). A charge pool left behind by an expired window still holds no slot (Resolved decision 1b).
- **No second HUD data path.** Rows keep coming from `EffectsRegistry` through `HUD.refresh()`; the label and panel derive from the same shared helper, never from a per-scene count.
- **No behaviour change below the cap.** Spawning, collection and choice behaviour with fewer than six held kinds must be identical.
- **Capture setups are not normal play.** If gating `sceneSetup.ts` would break scripted video scenes (AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB), document the divergence and its reason instead of leaving it silent.
- **Repository boundaries.** Only `src/` and `docs/` change; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.

## Existing state (verified in code, `dev`)

- **Slot model** (`src/powerups/slots.ts`): `resolveSlotState` builds `heldIds` from permanent power-up levels (`getLevels()`), permanent weapon **drop** levels (`getWeaponLevels()` filtered by `WEAPON_DROP_ID_SET`), active temporary power-up ids and temporary weapon drop ids; `used` = `[...heldIds].filter(countsTowardsSlotCap).length` where `countsTowardsSlotCap` excludes `availableWhenSlotsFull` entries (Extra Life, Mystery UFO — Q7a) and `SLOT_EXEMPT_UTILITY_DROP_IDS` (`reset`); `free` is clamped ≥ 0 and `isFull` is `used >= POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (6).
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`): `refresh()` renders one row per visible power-up (`_buildPowerUpRows()` + pre-existing visibility rules + `heldByModel` so a slot-held kind always gets a row) then one row per `registry.activeWeapons()`; `_drawSlotBudget()` shows `Loadout ${state.used}/${POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP}`; `_slotMarker()` marks non-slot rows `always available` (exempt) or `charges only` (anything else held only by a charge pool) — the marker is the only visual distinction.
- **Upgrade screen** (`src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` `YOUR UPGRADES` panel): rows from `buildOwnedLoadout(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` (`src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts`) — **permanent-only**, weapons first (drop ids minus `reset` minus `cannon`), then power-ups, each `level >= 1`; a consumable granted as a **charge** (not a level) holds level 0 and is absent from the panel (parent AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW AC1), while the HUD may still render its row via the consumable-ownership rule.
- **Known row classes that can render without a slot** (from AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX RCA + `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts`): exempt Mystery UFO row (`availableWhenSlotsFull`), Extra Life (no row — lives counter), Phase Shift / Teleport rows kept alive by residual charges after the 15 s temporary window expired (`charges only`).
- **Telemetry/recording evidence path**: `npm run record` → `scripts/record-session.mjs` writes a JSONL run (run_header, per-tick permanent levels via `PlayScene._telemetryExtras()`, `pickup`/`hold_full`/`choice_selected` events); `scripts/analyse-recording.mjs` and `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` read them (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`). The prior RCA used `recordings/six-slot.jsonl` (gitignored) the same way.

## Desired change

1. Establish the true cause from a recorded fresh-run session (or an equivalent scene test): classify each of the six visible rows as slot-counted or non-slot, and confirm what the label and the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel each counted.
2. If any surface lets a slot-counted kind be held without being counted (or counted without being held), fix it in the shared model/consumers and cover it with a regression test.
3. Make the player-visible loadout agree with the model: the label, the HUD rows and the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel must all read the same number of upgrades, and non-slot rows must be legible as non-slot (they are not upgrades).
4. Keep cap semantics intact (Q4a/Q5b/Q6a/Q7a, Resolved 1b, per-upgrade TTL AH-0MVUGI5P2001C1IL).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `resolveSlotState` / `resolvePlayerSlotState` / `countsTowardsSlotCap`; any missing predicate or invariant helper.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — `refresh()`, `_buildPowerUpRows()`, `_drawSlotBudget()`, `_slotMarker()`; where the visible row count and the `n/6` label must agree.
- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts` — `buildOwnedLoadout`; whether a charge-granted consumable should appear in `YOUR UPGRADES` and how it should be labelled.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — `_renderOwnedUpgradePanel()`; overlay presentation of the permanent loadout and non-slot kinds.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `openMineralChoice()` (ownedUpgrades wiring at L5597), `openMiniBossReward()` (unlock half), `_restoreCheckpoint()` (resume audit), `_telemetryExtras()` (permanent levels in telemetry).
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — capture/gym loadout application (audit or document divergence).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()`, `getPowerUpLevels()`, `getLevels()`, `getTempPowerUpIds()`, `getTempWeaponIds()`; the four snapshots.
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts`, `src/telemetry/schema.ts`, `scripts/record-session.mjs` — recording evidence path for AC1.
- `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`, `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.test.*` — existing coverage to extend.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (§ "The six loadout slots"), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 — cap semantics + HUD/overlay presentation docs.

## Related work

- **Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (HUD shows more than six equipped upgrades/weapons)** (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX, open) — the parent RCA for this row-class family; this report is the **under-count** direction (5 shown for 6 present) and must stay separate.
- **HUD six-slot budget and non-slot row marking** (AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR, completed) — introduced the `Loadout n/6` label and the `always available`/`charges only` markers; the surfaces this report is about.
- **HUD/slot agreement tests and reporting fixture** (AH-0MVVJRFDV007OI49, completed) — `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts`, the fixture replaying the recorded seven-rows-five-slots / six-slots-five-rows states.
- **On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades** (AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y, completed) — introduced the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel via `buildOwnedLoadout`.
- **Limit the number of powerup slots** (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF, completed) — parent feature; its ACs define the semantics to keep.
- **Temporary-inclusive six-slot cap with blocked-collection cue** (AH-0MVRCF584004SQFV, completed) — Q4a/Q5b semantics.
- **Permanent grant never strands a temporary stack** (AH-0MVUGI4IC006PUS5, completed) and **F7: per-upgrade TTL** (AH-0MVUGI5P2001C1IL, completed) — temporary-hold invariants that must stay green.
- **Power-ups and weapons both cumulative/leveled** (AH-0MUX802450085VZZ et al.) — the level store the snapshots read.
- **Scripted scenes for video** (AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, completed) and **Scripted-scene setup adoption** (AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8, completed) — `sceneSetup.ts` surface.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the sixth row the operator counted is a non-slot row (exempt Mystery UFO or residual Phase Shift/Teleport charge pool); the five slot-counted rows, the 5/6 label and the five permanent rows in `YOUR UPGRADES` then all agree with the model, and the bug is **presentation** (a non-slot row reads as an upgrade). If instead all six rows are slot-counted and the model still says 5, a genuine acquisition/accounting bug exists and AC2 becomes the primary fix.
- **Assumption:** the report is from a `dev` build containing the budget label and owned panel (commits 404c534f2, a998aacb5, on `dev`).
- **Risk — scripted-robot runs:** the `npm run record` evidence path usually needs a bot or manual play; if the operator has no recording, AC1 falls back to a scene test that assembles the six-row loadout through the real seams (as AH-0MVVJRFDV007OI49 did).
- **Risk — charge-grant vs level-grant presentation:** changing what `YOUR UPGRADES` lists for charge-granted consumables could surprise players who expect a "level"; keep any change minimal and documented.
- **Failure mode to expect, not a bug:** if AC1 shows a non-slot sixth row, the label and panel are already correct and AC3 (legible non-slot presentation / count agreement) is the substantive fix; report the AC1 classification before writing the fix so the two outcomes are not conflated.
- **Scope-creep risk:** redesigning the cap, changing which entries are exempt, re-labelling all rows, or reworking the choice overlay are out of scope — record them as `discovered-from:AH-0MVZ0GGW1004502H` items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where did your 'we had 6' count come from?" — Answer (operator): **(a)** counted the rows in the mid-run HUD upgrade list (6 rows visible). Source: interactive reply. Consequence: the HUD row list is the confirmed observation surface; the sixth row may be a non-slot row (the marker was not noticed — see Q3).
- Q2: "Which 'upgrade screen' showed 5?" — Answer (operator): **(a)** the hold-full mineral choice overlay (`YOUR UPGRADES` panel). Source: interactive reply. Consequence: the overlay's permanent-only panel is the second confirmed surface; a charge-granted consumable (level 0) or a temporary-only kind would legitimately be absent from it.
- Q3: "Among the 6 upgrade entries, was one visibly distinguished (e.g. marked `charges only` / `always available`, or a countdown while the rest showed ∞)?" — Answer (operator): **(c)** not sure / didn't notice. Source: interactive reply. Consequence: the non-slot-row hypothesis is neither confirmed nor refuted; AC1 requires the exact classification from a recording or fixture before deciding the fix direction. **OPEN QUESTION (follow-up if needed):** if the operator can still recall the run, the six Kinds (or a recording) would pin the classification directly.

# Gate Hangar War behind a feature flag (hidden until it works)

## Problem statement

The Hangar War outer loop (menu entry, hex-map attract traversal) is shipped in
every build — including production — but it currently doesn't work. Players can
reach a broken feature from the main menu, so the Hangar War entry surface must
be hidden behind a feature flag that is **off by default** until the feature is
fixed and the flag is deliberately turned on.

## Users & goals

- **Players** — must never land on a broken Hangar War from the shipped game's
  main menu. The classic 10-level campaign (Play Game / Continue / Watch Demo)
  is entirely unaffected either way.
- **Developers / capture pipeline** — need the cleanest possible way to keep
  exercising Hangar War screens (gyms, `npm run capture` bots, the open item
  "Ensure bot navigates Hangar War screens for npm run capture"
  (AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5)) without shipping the broken flow.

## Operator decisions (Intake interview, 2026-11-02)

1. **Scope of the gate ((b) chosen):** gate the **player-visible entry
   surfaces** only — the menu entry and the idle-attract Hangar War traversal —
   while **scenes stay registered** (`HangarScene`, `HexMapScene`,
   `DefenceReportScene` remain reachable via the dev gyms / `scene.start`), so
   the capture pipeline and gyms are unaffected by the flag.
2. **Flag mechanism and default ((b) chosen):** a **runtime toggle** persisted
   (e.g. `localStorage`, following `src/core/settingsStore.ts`'s
   merge-over-defaults pattern), **default OFF**, and the **ability to turn it
   ON is only available in dev mode** (`import.meta.env.DEV`). In a production
   build the flag is fixed OFF — no enable surface exists.
3. **Fixing Hangar War is out of scope here ((a) chosen):** this item is the
   gate only; making the feature work is tracked separately (see Related work).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`:
  - The `🛠  Hangar War` button (pointer + keyboard shift-tab/enter) starts
    `HangarScene` (`scene.start('HangarScene')`) — always rendered, always in
    the `FocusManager` cycle (AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I).
  - `scheduleAttractTimer` alternates the idle attract between the arcade demo
    and `startHangarWarDemo()` (the hex-map traversal) on an even/odd
    `demoCycleIndex` (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP).
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` registers `HangarScene` and `HexMapScene` in the
  scene array (unchanged by this item).
- **No feature-flag mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase** — the only
  env-style gate is `import.meta.env.DEV` for dev-only tooling (dev scenario,
  telemetry dev share, capture director, config write-back).
- Available precedent for a persisted dev-inert setting: `shareTelemetryDev` in
  `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — persisted in settings, but **inert outside a
  dev build** (the decision is made by the single dev gate in
  `src/telemetry/devMode.ts`).
- Notable defect (context for "doesn't work", **not** fixed here): a hex
  deployment ends in `DefenceReportScene` (`PlayScene.ts:5067`
  `scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, …)`), yet `DefenceReportScene` is
  **not registered** in `gameConfig`'s `scene` array — so the transition cannot
  resolve in a shipped build.

## Desired change

1. New persisted feature flag (default OFF), e.g. a `hangarWarEnabled` boolean
   in a settings-like store (or a new `featureFlags`-style module), with a
   single **effective-value resolver** that returns `false` in any
   non-dev build regardless of the stored value (production builds are inert —
   `import.meta.env.DEV === false` → flag OFF), mirroring the established
   `shareTelemetryDev` / `devMode.ts` pattern.
2. `MenuScene`:
   - Render the `🛠  Hangar War` button **only when the flag resolves ON**;
     when OFF it must be absent from both the scene and the `FocusManager`
     cycle (focus order preserved for the remaining controls).
   - In the idle-attract timer, run the Hangar War traversal only when the flag
     resolves ON; when OFF the attract alternation collapses to the shipped
     arcade demo only.
3. A **dev-only** enable surface (toggle in the dev settings UI or a
   `DEV`-gated control), so developers can explicitly turn the feature on for
   capture/gym work; the toggle itself is never present in a production build.
4. Tests: flag resolver unit tests (persist/load/default/corrupt/SSR-safe,
   production-inert), MenuScene tests for both flag states (button presence +
   focus order, attract traversal selection), and confirm gyms/registration are
   untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Effective flag resolver.** A persisted feature flag for the Hangar
  War is added, default OFF; the single resolver returns `false` in any
  non-dev build even when a stored value says otherwise (production inert),
  matching the `shareTelemetryDev`/dev-gate pattern. Unit tests cover default,
  persisted-ON, persisted-corrupt, SSR/no-storage and production builds.
- **AC2 — Menu entry hidden when OFF.** With the flag OFF, `MenuScene` shows no
  `🛠  Hangar War` control (no pointer or keyboard activation to it), the
  `FocusManager` cycle excludes it with the remaining controls' order
  unchanged, and Play Game / Continue / Watch Demo behave exactly as today.
- **AC3 — Attract traversal gated.** When the flag is OFF the idle-attract
  timer only ever starts the shipped arcade demo (no Hangar War traversal); the
  traversal selection is covered by a test at both flag states.
- **AC4 — Dev-only enable.** The ability to turn the flag ON exists only in dev
  mode (`import.meta.env.DEV`); a production build exposes no enable surface
  and the resolver still yields OFF.
- **AC5 — Scenes and gyms untouched.** `HangarScene`, `HexMapScene` and
  `DefenceReportScene` remain registered/reachable via the gyms and
  `scene.start`, and the dev-only enablement lets the capture pipeline and
  `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` keep working unchanged (parity matrix rows intact).
- **AC6 — Docs updated.** README menu description, GDD §2.1/§8.1/§8.2 entry
  surface text, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (unchanged-parity note) and any
  `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES` build-status remarks are updated to record the flag
  and its default-OFF production state.
- **AC7 — Suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- No changes to the shipped classic campaign flow or its checkpoint semantics.
- Scenes are **not** deregistered (decision (b)); gate entry surfaces only.
- No shared-core or gym↔game parity changes — the duplicate-body guard and
  parity docs remain green.
- Production builds must be fail-closed: stored value alone can never enable
  the feature.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** fixing Hangar War (incl. the unregistered
  `DefenceReportScene` defect) is deliberately out of scope (decision (a));
  the fix is tracked as a separate work item so this item stays a pure gate.
- **Dev-toggle leak risk:** a dev-only toggle must never reach a production
  build. Mitigation: a single resolver that is production-inert
  (`import.meta.env.DEV === false` → always OFF) plus an enforcement scan
  mirroring `src/telemetry/devModeEnforcement.test.ts`, and a bundle-hygiene
  marker check if a static-dist gate is desired.
- **Focus-order regression risk:** removing the Hangar War control must not
  disturb the remaining `FocusManager` cycle; covered by an explicit AC2 test.
- **Assumption:** the persisted flag lives in a settings-like store following
  `src/core/settingsStore.ts` merge-over-defaults (new field on
  `SettingsRecord` or a dedicated `featureFlags` module — implementer's
  choice, flagged in the comment).
- **Assumption:** "doesn't work" is real today and reproducible in the dev
  build via the menu entry; no separate reproduction is required to ship the
  gate (hiding the entry is correct regardless of the underlying cause).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (or new `src/core/featureFlags.ts`) — persisted
  flag field + resolver (default OFF, production-inert).
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — gate the Hangar War button + focus registration
  and the attract-traversal alternation on the resolver.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` (or menu dev area) — dev-only enable toggle
  (`import.meta.env.DEV`-gated).
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts`, new flag-resolver test — AC1–AC4 coverage.
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — AC6.

## Related work

- **Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment (AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I)** (completed) — created the entry this item gates.
- **Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP)** (completed) — created the attract traversal this item gates.
- **Ensure bot navigates Hangar War screens for npm run capture (AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5)** (open) — capture pipeline must keep working; dev-only enablement preserves it.
- **Build Candidate D — Hangar War … (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)** (open, high) — parent epic.
- **Fix Hangar War (tracked separately, per operator decision (a))** — the defect that motivated this gate; includes the unregistered `DefenceReportScene` finding above. Not addressed by this item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What should the flag hide when off — everything player-visible including
  scene registration (a), entry surfaces only with scenes staying registered
  and gyms reachable (b), or the menu entry only (c)?" — Answer (operator):
  **(b) entry surfaces only**. Recommendation offered: (a). Source: interactive
  reply, 2026-11-02.
- Q2: "What flag mechanism and default — build-time env var, default off in
  production/on in dev (a); runtime toggle persisted, default off, turn-on
  available only in dev (b); or committed constant default off (c)?" — Answer
  (operator): **(b) runtime toggle, default off, with the option to turn it on
  only available in dev mode**. Recommendation offered: (a). Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-02.
- Q3: "Is fixing Hangar War in scope here (gate only (a) vs gate + fix (b))?"
  — Answer (operator): **(a) gate only**; fixing tracked separately.
  Recommendation offered: (a). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-02.

discovered-from:AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP

# Goal

As a player, I want the Hangar War to actually work so its default-OFF feature flag (AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP) can be turned on (or removed) and the outer loop can ship again.

## Context

The Hangar War entry surfaces were gated behind `ai_hell_feature_flags.hangarWar` (default OFF, production-inert) in AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP because the feature currently does not work. That gate was deliberately scope-limited to entry surfaces; fixing the feature is tracked here.

## Known defect found during the gate implementation

- `PlayScene` ends a hex deployment by starting `DefenceReportScene` by key (`PlayScene.ts:5067`, `scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, …)`), but `DefenceReportScene` is **not registered** in the scene array in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — so the transition cannot resolve in a shipped build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Hangar War flow runs end to end in the shipped game with the feature flag ON: menu entry → hangar → hex map → deployment → defence report → hex map.
- The root cause of the reported breakage is identified and fixed (starting with the unregistered `DefenceReportScene`), with a regression test covering the transition.
- Deciding whether to keep the flag (turned on by default) or remove it is recorded on AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

data.description:
Release gate blocker discovered while running `/skill:ship release` (2026-11-02).

## Problem

`git add`/`git commit` failed with `error: object file .git/objects/d4/bf429... is empty` /
`fatal: unable to read tree`. `git fsck --full` reported 5 zero-length loose objects,
of which 3 pre-dated this session (mtime 2026-11-01 20:41) and 2 were created during
the failed commit attempt (mtime 2026-11-02 11:16).

This is a recurrence of the unclean-shutdown class of corruption recorded in
AH-0MVVNKP1B00701HR: an interrupted/crashed git write leaves 0-byte loose objects.
Corroborating evidence of an unclean stop in this repo:

- 6 stale worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` whose branches are all fully merged
  into `origin/dev` (no in-progress work items, no live pi sessions).
- A stale Code Freeze marker `.worklog/code-freeze.json` whose recorded `pid` (13824)
  now belongs to an unrelated process.

## Impact

The release could not proceed: `merge-dev-to-main.sh` aborts on a dirty tree, and the
failed commit left `dev` one commit ahead of `origin/dev` pointing at a corrupt tree.

## Recovery performed in this session

1. `git reset --hard 976c9d5cd` — discarded the unpersistable bookkeeping commit
   (its only content was a `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` timestamp refresh, which
   is regenerated automatically).
2. Deleted the 5 zero-length loose objects. Confirmed via `git rev-list --all --objects`
   that the 3 pre-existing corrupt objects were **unreachable** (no reachable commit,
   tree or blob referenced them), so no history was lost.
3. `git reflog expire --expire=now --expire-unreachable=now --all` plus
   `git gc --prune=now` to repack and drop the unreachable remnants of the failed
   commit (`.git` shrank 766 MB → 101 MB).
4. `git pull --ff-only origin dev` — `dev` now matches `origin/dev` (`a8791d42`).

Verification: `git fsck --no-progress` produces **no output** (no errors, no broken
links, no missing objects); `find .git/objects -type f -size 0` returns 0.

discovered-from:release (found blocking `/skill:ship release`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `git fsck --no-progress` in the main checkout reports no errors and no
  zero-length files remain under `.git/objects`. **Met** — fsck silent, 0 empty objects.
- AC2 — No reachable object was lost: the deleted corrupt objects were all unreachable
  and `dev`/`origin/dev` agree after repair. **Met** — `git rev-list --all --objects`
  showed zero reachability for the 3 legacy objects; `git status -sb` reports no
  divergence from `origin/dev`.
- AC3 — No work item was left orphaned `in-progress` and `dev` carries no
  unpersistable commit. **Met** — `wl in-progress --json` returns 0 items; `dev` HEAD
  is `a8791d42` (`origin/dev`).
- AC4 — The repository is healthy enough for the release pipeline to run: every
  repository-integrity precondition the pipeline depends on holds. Reaching `main` is a
  property of the release run, not of this recovery item, so it is deliberately **not**
  part of this AC.

  **Met.** Each item below is verifiable from the repository alone:

  1. `git fsck --no-progress` produces **no output** (no errors, no broken links, no
     missing objects). Verified 2026-11-02 after the repair.
  2. `find .git/objects -type f -size 0 | wc -l` → `0` (no zero-length loose objects).
  3. `git status --porcelain` → empty (the `merge-dev-to-main.sh` clean-worktree
     precondition at `merge-dev-to-main.sh:110` is satisfied).
  4. `git rev-parse dev` == `git rev-parse origin/dev` → `a8791d428...` (no unpushed or
     unpushed-unpersistable commit left on `dev`).
  5. `wl in-progress --json` → 0 items (no work item orphaned `in-progress` by the crash).
  6. `node <ship-skill>/scripts/check-unmerged-branches.js` → exit 0 and
     `node <ship-skill>/scripts/check-critical-items.js` → exit 0, where `<ship-skill>`
     resolves to the globally installed ship skill directory
     (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship`), i.e. the gate scripts are **not** part of this
     repository.
  7. Every top-level `in_review` item carries a readable audit (`wl audit-show <id>
     --json` returns a non-null `audit` object), i.e. the worklog store is readable end
     to end after the repair — no corruption-induced read failures.

## Session notes — release run narrative (informational, not acceptance criteria)

The release was then re-run on this repaired repository. It passed the
unmerged-branches, critical-items and worklog-ref gates, and its audit gates evaluated
the repaired store without any corruption or unreadable-store error. A pre-flight audit
refresh was executed from the globally installed ship skill at
`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (invoked as
`node ~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js --refresh-audits`); it reported
"20 refreshed, 8 still failing". Those 8 are all **child** items: 7 have parents that are
not `in_review` (out of release scope) or are covered by a passing `in_review` parent
audit, so they do not block the top-level gate; 1 is this item.

## Recommendations (not in scope of this item)

- Add a repo hygiene step to detect zero-length git objects (`find .git/objects -type f
  -size 0`) during `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.
- Audit the 6 stale worktrees and remove them once confirmed orphaned.
data.title: Recover AI_Hell git object store after unclean-shutdown corruption blocking release
